## Additional defect 3 — the same clock bug can destroy EPS's OWN parked pods

The `created_at` staleness clock (line 357) is not only a teammate hazard. For an
EPS-owned pod the ownership gate passes trivially (signal 1), so ANY `pod-<N>`
that is merely STOPPED — `pod.py stop`, the watcher's reversible auto-stop, a park
— is terminate-eligible at the next 09:37 run if it was CREATED >24h ago, with no
grace period at all. The only thing standing between a parked EPS pod and volume
destruction is the `keep-running` tag.

Live example at filing time: `pod-1739` (`yib7yjxjvmx6iz`) is EXITED and appears in
today's audit under `kept-exited` solely because task #1739 carries `keep-running`.
Remove that tag and the next run destroys the volume.

This mechanizes the hazard `.claude/rules/pod-config.md` already warns about
("a STOPPED volume is NOT durable", #1112) — the audit turns a reversible park into
an irreversible delete within <24h. The fix (measure from EXIT, not creation) closes
the teammate case and this one together, but the plan should state the EPS-side
case explicitly and test it.

## Additional defect 4 — zero alerting on an irreversible action

`pod_audit.py` has NO notification path (no telegram/push/alert call), and
`cron_pod_audit.sh` deliberately `exit 0`s even on rc=2 with the comment "we don't
want cron emails on every 'found and terminated stale pod' event". The only record
is `logs/pod_audit/YYYY-MM-DD.log`.

Every OTHER destructive fleet cron notifies: `vm_disk_guard.py`, `gcp_audit.py`, and
`autonomous_session_watch.py` all push. `pod_audit.py` is the sole destructive cron
that is silent — which is why 77 terminations across 14 days went unnoticed until a
teammate asked in chat.

Requirement: any auto-terminate must emit one push naming the pods destroyed. A
silent irreversible action on a SHARED account is the root reason this incident had
a 2-week detection lag.

## Near-miss worth encoding as a test — shared cluster infrastructure

The Anthropic fellows-cluster nodes were mis-attributed EPS-owned by signal 3 for at
least 13 consecutive days: `Anthropic 2-node-26-got` and `cluster-EUR-IS-pod-6/7/14`
carried `task #1112` in every audit log from 2026-07-22 through 2026-08-03
(`grep -hE "cluster-EUR-IS-pod|Anthropic 2-node" logs/pod_audit/*.log`). They
survived only because they were RUNNING (the `orphan-running` bucket is never
auto-terminated). Any one of them EXITing on an audit day would have destroyed a
fellows H200 cluster node — including the `cluster-EUR-IS` cluster that backs
`charmander`, the free `fellows` SLURM lane EPS itself dispatches to.

They are absent from the live team listing as of 2026-08-04 14:2x (cause unknown, NOT
our terminations — verified: no cluster/Anthropic name appears in any
`Terminating ...` block). The exposure returns if those nodes reappear in the team
account. Add a regression test: a pod whose name matches shared-cluster
infrastructure patterns is never terminate-eligible regardless of ownership signal.

## Fleet-surface audit — everything else checked CLEAN

The broken pair (`_scan_task_references` / `_is_eps_owned`) has NO other consumer:
`grep -rn "_is_eps_owned\|_scan_task_references" scripts/ src/` returns hits only in
`scripts/pod_audit.py`. Confirmed correctly scoped:

- `autonomous_session_watch.py` pod-safety pass — filters `_is_managed_pod(p)` AND
  requires `_issue_from_pod_name` to parse (line ~13709); auto-STOP is reversible;
  the #770 wedge terminate additionally carries the owner-liveness guard (#1667).
- `pod_lifecycle.cmd_terminate` (Step 8) — resolves by name via `_MANAGED_PREFIXES`
  (`pod-`, `epm-issue-`), plus the #1485 `keep-running` teardown shield.
- `backend_poll.py` auto-terminate paths — resolve via `get_pod_by_name` on EPS names.
- `gcp_audit.py` — dedicated project + `_MANAGED_NAME_PREFIX = "eps-issue-"` +
  `eps-cap-probe*` allowlist; every other instance is escalate-only, never deleted.
- `vm_disk_guard.py` / `clean_experiment_downloads.py` — the terminal-status gate is
  really implemented in code (`TERMINAL_CACHE_REAP_STATUSES`), not just documented;
  active-issue caches are escalate-only.
- HF Hub — no automated remote deletion; `delete_folder` appears only in the one-off
  `issue1108_repo_file_audit.py` recipes and a smoke-probe prefix cleanup.

Residual collision risk (design, not a live bug): a TEAMMATE pod named `pod-<N>`
would be destroyed by ordinary Step-8 teardown. Live check found exactly one
managed-prefix pod on the account and it is ours (`pod-1739`).
